title: Treasury Sanctions Major Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Terrorist Cartels
body: November 19, 2026 Coordinated Action with International Partners Targets a Cartel-Linked Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and Canadian-Based Mafia Leaders and Facilitators WASHINGTON —Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two international drug trafficking organizations: the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang ( Comancheros ) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta , a mafia-type criminal syndicate.  By providing essential logistical and operational support, the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta help terrorist cartels expand their international reach and sustain global narcotrafficking networks. “Cartels do not operate in isolation. They rely on other criminal organizations like the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta to move drugs, launder illicit proceeds, and ultimately poison Americans with narcotics,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will continue to expose and disrupt narcoterrorism networks to Keep America Safe.” The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering. The ‘Ndrangheta controls a significant share of the European cocaine trade, while the Comancheros have helped open access to some of the world's most lucrative illicit drug markets. In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans. Treasury has coordinated closely with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025.  OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons. Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks.  OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Homeland Security Investigations.  OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC worked closely with valued international partners, including the Australian Federal Police, New Zealand Police, Italy’s Guardia di Finanza, and Canada’s Royal Canadian Mounted Police and York Regional Police, whose cooperation was instrumental in supporting today’s action. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production. COMANCHERO OUTLAW MOTORCYCLE GANG Today, OFAC designated the Comancheros , also known as the Comanchero Motorcycle Club or simply Comanchero MC , an Australian drug trafficking organization with an international footprint in Asia, Europe, and North America.  Developing strategic partnerships with U.S. sanctioned cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Clan del Golfo, and Los Choneros, the Comancheros have facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram shipments of cocaine from South America to the United States, Australia, and Europe.  The Comancheros have also been involved in other criminal activity around the world, including assassinations, arms trafficking, and money laundering. Because Australia and New Zealand are some of the world’s most lucrative illicit drug markets, Mexican cartels are increasingly targeting these markets to capitalize on the significantly higher margins and growing demand.  Due to the geographic distance from the major cocaine producing regions in the Western Hemisphere, cartels can charge substantial premiums compared to drugs sold in the United States.  The Sinaloa Cartel has been known to send “sleeper cells” to Australia to facilitate local drug distribution and establish contacts with the Comancheros and other outlaw motorcycle gangs who assist with the logistics of drug trafficking. The Comancheros are being designated under E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. COMANCHERO COMMAND AND CONTROL Alexandre Varela Villar , better known as Alex Vare ( Vare ), is the Spain-based World Commander of the Comancheros. Allan John Norman Meehan , better known as Allan Meehan ( Meehan ), is the Australia-based World President of the Comancheros. Pasilika Naufahu ( Pasilika ) is the national president of the New Zealand chapter of the Comancheros.  Before being deported to New Zealand in 2016, Pasilika was the sergeant-at-arms of the Comancheros in Australia.  Pasilika was arrested and sentenced to 10 years in prison in February 2021 for various charges related to his position in the Comancheros.  In close coordination with his brother and senior Comancheros member, Vetekina Naufahu ( Vetekina ), Pasilika has facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram importations of drugs into New Zealand and has established connections to the Sinaloa Cartel. Marco Francis Coffen ( Coffen ) is an associate of the Comancheros and has been involved in supplying multiple Australian criminal organizations, including the Comancheros, with encrypted communication platforms to drug traffickers and shielding them from police phone taps. Vare and Meehan are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for being or having been leaders or officials of the Comancheros. Pasilika and Vetekina are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Comancheros. Coffen is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the Comancheros. OMERTÀ – THE ‘NDRANGHETA The ‘Ndrangheta , an international drug trafficking organization and mafia-type criminal syndicate, operates in over 80 countries and continues to grow.  The ‘Ndrangheta’s adherence to omertà , a code of silence, and its reliance on deeply rooted familial bloodlines have enabled the organization to maintain secrecy, foster loyalty, resist infiltration, and expand its criminal influence across generations and international borders.  While the ‘Ndrangheta was founded in Calabria, Italy, the organization has expanded across Europe, the Western Hemisphere, and Australia.  As one of the largest criminal organizations in the world, the ‘Ndrangheta’s primary business comes from drug trafficking, with some estimates stating that almost 80 percent of the European cocaine trade is controlled by the ‘Ndrangheta.  While primarily focused on the cocaine trade, Italian officials have stated that the ‘Ndrangheta have started expanding into the illicit fentanyl market. The ’Ndrangheta frequently partner with Mexican and South American drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, and Clan del Golfo.  In the past, the ‘Ndrangheta has also partnered with other Mexican drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including Los Zetas (now known as Cartel del Noreste) and the Gulf Cartel. The ‘Ndrangheta was previously designated on May 30, 2008 , pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act).  Today, the ‘Ndrangheta is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. ‘NDRANGHETISTI NORTH OF THE BORDER Locali (singular: locale ) are the primary territorial organizational unit of the ‘Ndrangheta, comprising members known as ‘ ndranghetisti , that oversee and coordinate criminal activities within a specific geographical region.  The ‘Ndrangheta locale that operates in the Greater Toronto Area in Canada has strengthened in recent years, becoming so powerful that they dictate events in Italy from across the ocean.  In Canada, the ‘Ndrangheta is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and other crimes.  This faction of the ‘Ndrangheta uses the U.S. and Canadian financial systems to launder illicit proceeds. Today, OFAC designated Italian-born Angelo Figliomeni (also known as “Don Angelino”), the leader of the Toronto faction of the ‘Ndrangheta.  A member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina (family), Angelo Figliomeni fled to Canada in the early 2000’s to escape a 20-year sentence for weapons charges in Italy.  Angelo’s power extends beyond Canada, stretching back to Italy.  He has engaged in money laundering and other criminal activities on behalf of the ‘Ndrangheta. Another member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina is Italian-born Cosimo Figliomeni (sometimes known as “Cosimino”), who is a top leader of the ‘Ndrangheta faction in Toronto and has been the subject of criminal proceedings in Italy in connection to his role within the ‘Ndrangheta organization. OFAC also designated two members of the Commisso ‘ndrina who are long time Italian-born leaders of the ‘Ndrangheta in Toronto. Francesco Commisso , also known as “U Scelto,” has faced allegations in Italy of being part of a Toronto oversight body that was tasked, among other duties, with imposing disciplinary sanctions on members. Rocco Remo Commisso (also known as Remo Commisso ) is a Canada-based leader of the ‘Ndrangheta and leads narcotics trafficking networks within the United States, including in the state of New York.  Remo Commisso was convicted in Canada in 1981 for conspiracy to commit murder and again in 1984 for his involvement in a bombing that killed one person.  Remo Commisso is involved in narcotics trafficking in the United States for the ‘Ndrangheta, including in New York. Vincenzo DeMaria (also known as Jimmy DeMaria ) is one of Toronto’s top ‘Ndrangheta bosses and has been active in the Toronto organized crime scene for decades.  DeMaria shot and killed a man in 1981 over a $2,000 drug debt and was convicted of second-degree murder in 1982.  He has since been released from prison and holds significant power in the ‘Ndrangheta. Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Jimmy DeMaria make up the Camera di Controllo of Toronto, a collegial body of the ‘Ndrangheta that decides on important questions concerning the organization and settles disputes, even outside of Toronto.  The Toronto ‘Ndrangheta is tightly connected throughout the world and has close relationships with members back in Calabria. Luigi Vescio Sr. (also known as “The Undertaker” or “Lui Vescio”) is a Canadian-born ‘Ndrangheta senior member and associate of Angelo Figliomeni and Jimmy DeMaria. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Luigi Vescio Sr. were all charged in the Italian Court of Reggio Calabria for mafia-type association related to their leadership, membership, and promotion of the ‘Ndrangheta in 2019. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, Jimmy DeMaria, and Luigi Vescio Sr. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, ‘Ndrangheta. FAMILY-OWNED, MAFIA-CONNECTED – VESCIO FUNERAL HOMES OFAC is also designating the corporate network of Vescio Sr., including his network of funeral homes in Ontario.  These funeral homes include the Fratelli Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Woodbridge, Ontario, Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Toronto and Vescio Funeral Home (Maple) Inc. in Maple, Ontario.  Vescio Sr. also controls a Toronto-based luxury limousine rental business, Phantom Limousine Services Inc. Vescio Sr. serves as the president of each of these companies. OFAC is also designating Luigi Vescio Sr.’s wife, Rose Vescio , and his two children, Luigi Vescio Jr. and Laura Vescio , for their roles in owning and operating the Vescio Funeral Homes on behalf of Luigi Vescio Sr. Rose Vescio, Luigi Vescio Jr., and Laura Vescio are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Luigi Vescio Sr. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . title: Treasury Targets Cyber Scam Operators and Armed Group Facilitators in Southeast Asia
body: November 19, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned three individuals involved in operating and facilitating cyber scam centers in Southeast Asia, as well as two affiliated companies.  The individuals designated today include operators of scam compounds that target Americans through virtual currency investment fraud and affiliates of armed groups that provide protection and support to scam-center networks in Southeast Asia. “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury has aggressively targeted overseas scam compounds to protect Americans from fraud,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “We will continue to use all available tools to disrupt and dismantle the networks that enable scam compounds to operate.” These actions are being taken in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. Government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  Today’s action further reflects OFAC’s coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center.  OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). ZHAO HUI: A SCAM CENTER OPERATOR Zhao Hui (Zhao) is a Cambodian national who leased a scam center owned by the OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO and paid protection fees to the OFAC-designated leader of the Prince Group TCO, Chen Zhi .  In addition, Zhao owned a scam compound in Cambodia independent of Prince Group TCO.  At this scam compound, Zhao was directly involved in scam operations and managed this scam compound’s leases.  This scam compound primarily targeted Americans and Europeans.  Such scam compounds conduct virtual currency investment scams.  Since Zhao has leased a scam compound and owned and operated an additional scam compound in Cambodia, he has materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of virtual cryptocurrency investment scams, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is the chairman of the board of directors of Cambodia-based construction company Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration Co., Ltd . (Bei Fang Bo Lin) and management and consultancy company ZHZ Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (ZHZ Investment). Bei Fang Bo Lin and ZHZ Investment are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Zhao Hui. THE DKBA’S FACILITATION OF SCAM COMPOUND ACTIVITY In recent years, armed groups in Burma have transformed a strip along the Thai-Burmese border into one of the world’s highest concentrations of scam centers.  The Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA) is an ethnic armed group previously designated by OFAC for supporting cyber scam centers in Burma that target Americans using fraudulent investment schemes.  DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds. Since December 2025, General Saw Shwe Wah has been the commander-in-chief of the DKBA, replacing General Saw Steel , who OFAC designated in November 2025 pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. Colonel Saw A One is the DKBA commander who oversees security in the Three Pagodas Pass in Karen State near the Thai border.  The region has seen expansion of new buildings intended for telecom scam operations, with many scam actors entering the area with the assistance of the DKBA, which also protects them.  Saw A One reportedly owns a plantation where scam operations occur and has contracted for scam operations. Saw Shwe Wah and Saw A One are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being or having been leaders, officials, senior executive officers, or members of the board of directors of the DKBA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. title: Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection Issues Annual Consumer Advisory on Holiday Scams
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP) released its annual holiday advisory to help consumers protect themselves from the seasonal surge in cyber-enabled scams and online fraud. As frauds and scams continue to proliferate, including through the use of super intelligence, it is important to remember that anyone can be a victim of fraud. Learn how to identify fraudulent activity, disrupt scammers, and report incidents quickly to keep yourself and others safe. This holiday season, Treasury urges consumers to stay vigilant, be proactive, and respond quickly if they believe they are being targeted. Share your stories and experiences with your community to help teach others how to stay safe from scams. "As cybercriminals increasingly leverage super intelligence (SI) to carry out more sophisticated and convincing scams, it is more important than ever for Americans to remain vigilant this holiday season." said Cory Wilson, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection.  "Cybercriminals are exploiting SI to impersonate trusted individuals, businesses, and even loved ones, putting Americans and their hard-earned money at risk.  Treasury remains committed to strengthening consumer resilience against cyber-enabled fraud through education, awareness, and actionable guidance. We encourage all Americans to take a moment to verify suspicious requests, recognize the warning signs of fraud, and report all suspected scams to the appropriate authorities." Access OCCIP’s Staying Cyber-Safe this Holiday Season . Report fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and the Federal Bureau of Investigation Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . ###

title: Treasury International Capital Data for September
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for September 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for October 2026, is scheduled for December 15, 2026. The sum total in September of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $261.0 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $267.0 billion, and net foreign official outflows were $6.0 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in September; their net purchases were $186.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $148.3 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $38.4 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $31.4 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $155.3 billion in September. Foreign residents increased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $3.5 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $2.9 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents increased by $108.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Proxy Networks
body: November 18, 2026 Targets Include Hizballah-Affiliated Charity, Gold and Cash Smuggling Network WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Wa Ta’awanu Association (Wa Ta’awanu), a Hizballah-affiliated charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. OFAC today also designated members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network run by Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). “The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies.” Today’s action exposes Hizballah’s continued exploitation of civilian charitable organizations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance.  It also increases pressure on the group’s illicit financing networks as Hizballah seeks to resist growing calls and international pressure to disarm. Today’s action is being taken pursuant to the United States’ counterterrorism authority, Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended.  The U.S. Department of State designated Hizballah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to E.O. 13224 on October 31, 2001, for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States.  Previously, the U.S. Department of State had designated Hizballah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act on October 8, 1997.  OFAC also designated Hizballah pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the IRGC-QF. HIZBALLAH’S ABUSE OF THE CHARITABLE SECTOR Hizballah-affiliated Wa Ta’awanu is a Lebanon-based charity that provides emergency relief services for southern Lebanon while also channeling outside donor funds toward Hizballah’s terrorist activities.  In July 2026, as part of the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure those areas and ensure that they were free from Hizballah fighters and weapons.  However, Wa Ta’awanu provides a pretext for Hizballah’s militant activities in the pilot zones, preventing disarmament and inhibiting Lebanese government efforts to safeguard these areas.  Wa Ta’awanu founder Afif Abdel Rida Chouman leads the charity and coordinates the organization’s activities at Hizballah’s direction. Wa Ta’awanu and Afif Abdel Rida Chouman are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah. HIZBALLAH GOLD AND CASH NETWORK In coordination with Hizballah financial officials, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen have transferred significant funds over the course of their operations from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen is the owner of Lebanon-based Gold Global Company , which he uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen’s network also employs couriers to transfer funds in cash across borders.  Hassan Khechen’s brother, Ibrahim Khechen, also participates in Hizballah’s money smuggling network and has links to a related courier who was arrested in February 2025 at the Beirut airport with $2.5 million in his hand luggage.  Türkiye-based and Hizballah-affiliated Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), also controlled by Hassan Khechen, assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah.  Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hassan Khechen. title: November 18, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease For Immediate Release: November 18, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds). Infilbray crosses the blood-brain barrier to reduce the accumulation of harmful substances in the body and brain. “For patients with Type 3 Gaucher disease, harmful substances build up in the brain without a way to stop them, but this drug's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier means it can get to the source of the buildup driving the neurological symptoms,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “This approval reflects the FDA’s commitment to advancing therapeutic options for patients with rare diseases and brings an important new treatment to patients and the healthcare providers who care for them.” GD3 is a rare, inherited condition in which the body cannot properly break down fatty substances, called glucosphingolipids, due to a deficient or malfunctioning enzyme. As these substances accumulate in organs, tissues, and the brain, patients experience a wide range of serious health problems over time. Unlike type 1 Gaucher disease, GD3 also affects the brain and nervous system, causing difficulties with balance, coordination, speech, memory, and thinking — symptoms that can worsen progressively and significantly impact quality of life. Infilbray works as a glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, reducing the buildup of harmful substances throughout the body and, critically, within the brain. The FDA’s approval of Infilbray is supported by data from a randomized, double-blind, multicenter clinical study enrolling 43 patients aged 12 years and older with GD3 who had previously been treated with enzyme replacement therapy and had achieved systemic disease stabilization. Participants received either Infilbray orally once daily or intravenous enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks for 52 weeks. Treatment effectiveness was evaluated using two assessments that capture the neurological symptoms central to daily life in patients with GD3, including those related to ataxia (loss of muscle control and coordination) and cognitive function. At Week 52, patients treated with Infilbray demonstrated improvement on a measure that combined both assessments compared to those taking enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of non-neurologic manifestations of GD3. The most frequently reported side effects of Infilbray include gastrointestinal symptoms as well as adverse effects on mood. Serious psychiatric risks, including suicidal ideation and behavior, have been reported. Potential risks identified from animal studies include potential clouding of vision in younger patients and adverse effects on fetal development when drug is taken during pregnancy. More information on side effects can be found in the drug labeling. Infilbray was granted Orphan Drug designation as well as Priority Review . The approval of Infilbray was granted to Genzyme Corporation, a Sanofi Company. title: FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
body: November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements, which are integral to efforts to combat money laundering and counter the financing of terrorism. FinCEN issues this proposal as a part of Treasury’s implementation of Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America’s Financial System . “Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our financial systems from criminal organizations and cartels that target law-abiding businesses and workers,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “This proposed rule cuts unnecessary burden, gives institutions more flexibility to effectively combat risk, and strengthens our fight against financial crime.” The proposed rule would amend customer due diligence requirements to: explicitly provide that covered financial institutions can obtain additional information about beneficial owners of a legal entity customer that may be useful in mitigating risk or addressing supervisory concerns; codify exceptive relief FinCEN issued removing the requirement for covered financial institutions to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal entity customer each time the customer opens a new account; and specify information that a covered financial institution must obtain about each beneficial owner of a legal entity customer. FinCEN welcomes public comments. The comment period closes 60 days after the proposed rule’s publication in the Federal Register . Resources Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Fact Sheet ###

title: Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement
body: November 17, 2026 SECURE 2.0 Final Regulations Expand Automatic Enrollment in Workplace Retirement Plans WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today issued final regulations to help more Americans save for retirement through their workplaces. The regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act, providing employers with clear guidance on automatic enrollment for certain 401(k) and 403(b) retirement plans. The rules help workers build retirement savings while preserving their control over how much they contribute. Treasury estimates that SECURE 2.0’s automatic enrollment expansion provision will increase retirement savings by an average of $4.2 billion annually over the 2023-2032 period. “A financially secure retirement is a cornerstone of the American Dream, and every worker deserves the opportunity to achieve it,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s rules help more American families and workers build retirement savings while keeping them in control of their contributions, and give employers the clarity and flexibility to invest in their employees’ futures.” “With the SECURE 2.0 regulations in place, American families will be able to boost their savings and keep more of their hard-earned money through their automatic enrollment in a retirement account,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “These regulations reduce the administrative burden placed on taxpayers when making long-term financial decisions. More broadly, they further the IRS goal of improving taxpayer service by making interactions with the Service simpler and easier.” STRENGTHENING AMERICANS’ RETIREMENT SAVINGS The final regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act by clarifying requirements for plan sponsors and simplifying certain participant notices. Covered retirement plans generally must automatically enroll eligible employees at a contribution rate of three percent. After an initial participation period, the default contribution rate must generally increase by at least one percentage point each year until it reaches at least ten percent, subject to a fifteen percent maximum. Employees may opt out or choose a different contribution rate. The final regulations generally apply to retirement plan years beginning after December 31, 2027, giving employers time to make necessary administrative changes. The final regulations: Clarify statutory exceptions for qualifying small and new businesses, governmental plans, church plans, and SIMPLE 401(k) plans; Give employers flexibility in the timing and amount of automatic contribution increases, within statutory limits; Simplify plan communications by allowing certain required notices to be combined and reducing annual notice requirements for qualifying employees who are not participating, provided they receive annual reminders and any plan documents they are entitled to request; and Explain how automatic enrollment requirements apply following plan mergers. The final regulations are available here . ###

title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), a landmark initiative that will fundamentally transform how the FDA's regulatory drug and biologic approval decisions are leveraged by health authorities around the world. The GRDP marks a major step forward in the FDA's global leadership and may accelerate patient access to innovative therapies throughout the world. The GRDP enables the FDA to more efficiently share minimally redacted approval packages, including the FDA's detailed scientific and regulatory assessments, directly with companies who can then share them with regulatory authorities outside of the United States, empowering those authorities to rely on the FDA's rigorous, science-based review decisions rather than conducting duplicative and time-consuming product evaluations of their own, while maintaining sovereignty over their regulatory decision. "The GRDP is a prime example of America First policies improving public health worldwide," said Grace Graham, FDA Deputy Commissioner for Policy, Legislation, and International Affairs . "The FDA is the global gold standard and making it easier for applicants to leverage our detailed scientific assessments to facilitate faster access for patients everywhere is an example of America’s continued interest in advancing global health under the Trump Administration." The GRDP launched on Oct. 30, with a President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) tentative approval for lenacapavir , a drug indicated for both HIV prevention and treatment. This is an especially meaningful starting point given PEPFAR's life-saving mission to combat HIV/AIDS in some of the world's most vulnerable populations. The GRDP is currently available to PEPFAR tentative approvals, excluding tentatively approved abbreviated new drug application products. However, the FDA intends to expand the GRDP in January 2027 to all novel drug and biologics (New Molecular Entity New Drug Applications and 351(a) Biologics License Applications), dramatically broadening the program's reach and impact. The FDA also intends to launch a pathway in early 2027 to expedite an applicant’s ability to request their minimally redacted action packages for approved and licensed drugs and biologics, accelerating global access to medicines that are already on the market in the United States and have been found to be safe and effective by the FDA. To receive a minimally redacted application approval package as part of the GRDP, applicants must request to participate within 10 calendar days of approval and confirm the application package is being submitted to a foreign regulatory authority in support of a marketing application. Applicants with eligible GRDP applications will receive detailed information in FDA approval letters and the agency intends to provide the minimally redacted package on an expedited basis. Requests for minimally redacted approval packages for other purposes will not be processed under the GRDP and should be submitted as a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request. “In an era of increasing global interdependence in pharmaceutical development and supply chains, the FDA's leadership is most effective when it is collaborative,” said Mark Abdoo, FDA Associate Commissioner for Global Policy and Strategy . “The GRDP reflects a forward-looking vision of regulatory leadership: one defined not by exclusivity, but by the willingness to share expertise, elevate global standards, and put patients first — wherever they are.” The GRDP addresses one of the most persistent and consequential challenges in global health: the gap between regulatory approval in high-capacity countries and patient access in lower-resource settings. When a drug is approved by the FDA, patients in many parts of the world may wait months or years longer for their own national health authority to complete an independent review due to limited regulatory capacity and resources. Beyond individual product approvals, the GRDP supports global health security. Harmonized regulatory decisions reduce the risk of fragmented or inconsistent product standards across markets, helping to ensure that the same high-quality therapies reach patients regardless of where they live, including here in the United States. title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer New therapy offers a meaningful treatment option for families facing a rare and serious childhood disease For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first treatment shown to help people with a severe form of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) live longer. Lembaz is approved to reduce the risk of death in adult and pediatric patients who weigh at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) and whose neurological symptoms began before age 6, also known as infantile-onset NPC. “For families living with Niemann-Pick disease type C, today’s approval marks an important milestone,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “For the first time, there is a treatment shown to help adults and children with this serious disease live longer, and we are committed to continuing to support the development of therapies for the rare disease community.” Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) is a rare, inherited lysosomal storage disorder affecting an estimated 1 in 150,000 people, in which the body cannot properly process cholesterol and other fats inside cells. Over time, these substances accumulate — particularly in the brain — causing progressive neurological decline, including loss of movement, coordination, and the ability to swallow. Patients whose neurological symptoms begin before age 6 face the most serious form of the disease. Prior to this approval action, two therapies were approved for NPC, but neither has been shown to reduce the risk of death. Both carry age and weight restrictions that limit access for the youngest and most seriously affected patients. Lembaz is the first FDA-approved therapy to reduce the risk of death in adults and children weighing at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) with NPC whose neurological symptoms began before age 6. A trained healthcare provider gives Lembaz as an injection directly into the spinal canal — a procedure called an intrathecal injection — every two weeks. To assess whether Lembaz reduced the risk of death, the FDA examined the survival of 36 patients treated with Lembaz across three clinical studies and an expanded access program. All patients had neurological manifestations of NPC that occurred prior to age 6. Patients treated with Lembaz had longer overall survival compared to the matched external control group, with a 55% reduction in the risk of death. The median survival time was 8.5 years for the treated group compared with 4.9 years in the control group. This survival benefit was observed regardless of whether patients were also taking miglustat, a therapy used off-label in NPC. The most common side effects of Lembaz include problems with hearing, balance and coordination, fatigue, vomiting, back pain, headache, fever, diarrhea, nausea, and cough. Lembaz carries a boxed warning for hearing impairment, including permanent hearing loss. A comprehensive hearing evaluation should be performed on patients before starting Lembaz and regularly throughout treatment, and dose adjustments may be needed based on the results of these evaluations. Lembaz received Breakthrough Therapy designation. The FDA granted approval of Lembaz to Mandos, LLC, a subsidiary of Beren Therapeutics, PBC. title: Treasury Sanctions Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Mexican Narco-Terrorist Cartels
body: November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned the Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization (DTO) and the Los Huistas DTO for supporting Mexico’s largest narco-terrorist groups, the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), which the Trump Administration has designated as both Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs) last year.  Based in Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO control strategic trafficking corridors along the borders with Honduras and Mexico, making them indispensable logistics partners for the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG. “Today’s action exposes the ties between politically influential Guatemalan criminal organizations and Mexican foreign terrorist organizations that facilitate the flow of deadly narcotics into the United States,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Under President Trump’s America First agenda, the Treasury Department will continue to target the criminal networks that enable violent organizations like the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG to traffic drugs across our borders and threaten the safety of the American people.” The Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO facilitate the receipt, storage, protection, and cross-border movement of narcotics destined for the United States and other international markets.  Through longstanding alliances spanning Central and South America, the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG have expanded their criminal operations, established sophisticated cross-border trafficking networks, and consolidated control over critical segments of the illicit drug supply chain.  By targeting these key facilitators, OFAC is disrupting critical nodes in the supply chains that enable the trafficking of fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, and other illicit drugs throughout the region. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, “E.O.13224, as amended”), which targets terrorists and their supporters. This action was done in coordination with the Department of State who is taking action against narcoterrorists destabilizing the Western Hemisphere.  In a concurrent action, the Department of State is also designating Los Lorenzanas as both an FTO pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and as an SDGT pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended. SINALOA CARTEL AND CJNG: LEVERAGING GUATEMALAN ALLIANCES TO FACILITATE DRUG TRAFFICKING Today, OFAC is sanctioning Los Mendoza DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059 and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel.  Additionally, OFAC is sanctioning Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG.  In Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO play important roles in facilitating narco-trafficking activities by controlling strategic trafficking corridors along the country’s borders with Honduras and Mexico.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG collaborate with local criminal groups like Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO to manage key logistical operations, including the receipt, storage, and cross-border transportation of narcotics, in order to move narcotics into Mexico for distribution in the United States and other international markets. The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG are the most powerful cartels in Mexico and responsible for a significant portion of deadly drugs trafficked into the United States.  In addition to trafficking fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, and other illicit drugs into the United States, these cartels have engaged in widespread violence and other criminal endeavors, such as fuel theft and timeshare fraud.  On February 20, 2025 , the Department of State designated both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG as FTOs and SDGTs.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG were each also identified by the United States as significant foreign narcotics traffickers on April 15, 2009 and on April 8, 2015 , respectively, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act. On December 15, 2021 , OFAC also designated the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG pursuant to E.O. 14059. LOS MENDOZA AND LOS HUISTAS DTOS – KEY LOGISTICS PARTNERS Founded in the 1980s, Los Mendoza DTO is one of Guatemala’s oldest and most powerful criminal organizations.  The family-based organization operates as a key transportation and logistics intermediary for the Sinaloa Cartel, facilitating drug trafficking operations across Guatemala and Honduras.  Los Mendoza DTO supports the Sinaloa Cartel’s trafficking network by facilitating access to border crossings, clandestine airstrips, storage facilities, and local protection networks in the Guatemalan departments of San Marcos, Huehuetenango, and Peten.  Beyond narcotics trafficking, Los Mendoza DTO is involved in contract killings and money laundering, and has amassed significant economic interests through land dispossession, cattle ranching, agricultural businesses, and real estate investments across Peten, Izabal, and Guatemala’s border region with Mexico. Active since the 1990s, Los Huistas DTO is one of Guatemala’s most powerful and longstanding criminal organizations.  Los Huistas DTO serves as a critical link in the cocaine trafficking supply chain from South America through Mexico and ultimately into the United States.  On March 18, 2022, OFAC designated Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059.  Los Huistas DTO maintains operational ties with both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG, providing logistical support and protection for narcotics shipments.  Los Huistas DTO’s longstanding ties to local businessmen, law enforcement officials, and politicians have enabled it to dominate the underworld in parts of northwestern Guatemala.  Through these relationships, Los Huistas DTO has cultivated political influence and institutional access which have facilitated its criminal operations and helped to shield the organization from the purview of law enforcement. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s (FinCEN’s) whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the entities designated today. ###

title: Remarks from Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations Gala
body: November 11, 2026 As prepared for delivery. Thank you, Evan [Greenberg], for that introduction, and for the invitation to be here. It gives me great pleasure to join you on this occasion. More than as representatives of the world’s largest economies, we meet tonight as stewards of one of this century’s most consequential relationships. Of course, when this Committee was formed in 1966, the Pacific was only the most visible distance between the United States and China. Formal diplomatic ties were still over a decade away. Our governments rarely spoke. And our people, likewise, rarely met. But a “small, loosely cohesive” band of China watchers believed that distance was reason to know more, not less. And so, they set out to understand China more deeply and to engage with it more seriously. They could not anticipate where exactly the relationship would lead, only that it would matter. The founders of this Committee set for themselves the ambitious task of reaching all segments of society—“from the layman, through the specialist, to the policy maker”—and “forging enduring links” between them. Tonight, sixty years later, take one look around this room, and you can see how fully their ambition has been realized. The United States and China represent different systems. Our national interests often diverge. But the links that you have built now bind generations and cultures together. They reach public servants and private citizens. Scholars who are bringing new ideas to light and entrepreneurs who are putting new ideas into practice. On both sides of the Pacific, people understand each other better because the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations brought them together. So, before I go any further, let me recognize two men who embody the best of this work. Steve Orlins has devoted much of his professional life to the U.S.-China relationship. He was part of the team that established diplomatic relations in the 1970s and then spent decades strengthening the ties that sustain them. Steve, you leave behind a legacy of great consequence, for which I offer my sincere thanks and congratulations. I am also pleased to acknowledge our second honoree. If Steve Orlins has shaped the history of our engagement with China, Stephen Schwarzman has made a transformative investment in its future. By founding the Schwarzman Scholars program, he has carried forward the conviction that animates this Committee. Relationships between nations are built on relationships between people. Steve, a new generation of leaders will be better prepared to navigate the U.S.-China relationship because you have given them the chance to understand it—and one another—more deeply. Congratulations. Now, while this Committee has supported bilateral relations for decades, the truth is that the ties between us span centuries. In fact, our relationship with China is nearly as old as the republic itself. In the winter of 1784, before we had a president—before we even had a constitution—an American ship, the Empress of China, departed New York Harbor and turned her bow toward the Pearl River. The vessel carried American crew and cargo, and with them, the confidence of a young country that had won its independence and was already reaching for a place among the great trading nations of the world. Major Samuel Shaw, who later served as the first American consul to China, recalled that upon the ship’s arrival, the Chinese people “were highly pleased at the prospect of so considerable a market for the productions of theirs.” Two nations, once separated by great distance, were drawn together by the possibilities of exchange. So before Washington and Beijing had ambassadors, we had merchants. Before our envoys learned how to engage, our people had already discovered how to do business. And before diplomacy gave this relationship its shape, the flow of goods gave it its force. Shaw celebrated that flow of commerce in both directions. And he was clear about the terms on which that commerce should proceed: “in all cases equal.” Even then, Americans expected a fair footing. Nearly two and a half centuries have passed since the Empress made her maiden voyage. What began with a single American ship bound for Canton—what began with the trading of ginseng for porcelain, tea, and silk—has matured into a vast trading network between the world’s two largest economies. Of course, the world that Samuel Shaw inhabited has long receded into history. But the instinct that carried him across an ocean endures. Americans still seek now what we sought then, which is to pursue opportunity wherever it lies, and to insist on fairness wherever we compete. Trade must advance the interests of both parties without diminishing the sovereignty of either. And it is precisely in that spirit that President Trump has approached our relationship with China. Today, U.S.-China relations are defined by the relationship between our two leaders. From the time of his first election, President Trump has, in his own words, “forged a friendship [with President Xi] built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people.” That friendship has brought unprecedented direct engagement between the leaders of our two nations, which I try to extend to the working level. Of course, in May, President Trump traveled to Beijing. In September, President Xi came to Washington. And next week, I will join President Trump in Shenzhen, where the two leaders will meet before a fourth encounter in Miami. These meetings are historic in their frequency. Never before have our leaders engaged face-to-face so often in a single year. But more significant is the understanding they are helping to establish. President Trump and President Xi agree that the United States and China should build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity. And they’ve chartered two new institutions in service of those objectives. Under the Board of Trade, we reached consensus to identify more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction. The board also launched a working group to address trade barriers in the agricultural sector. And previously, China agreed to import at least 25 million metric tons of soybeans and 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States over the next two years. The Board of Investment, meanwhile, provides a structured forum for commercially meaningful issues, like market access for American companies and increased predictability for Chinese companies. And these initiatives are part of our broader work to advance a fair and reciprocal relationship with China. They give practical expression to the principle at the core of President Trump’s agenda, which is to measure the success of American engagement abroad by what it delivers here at home. By how it advances the prosperity of our people. Strengthens the resilience of our economy. And safeguards the security of our nation. Of course, the U.S. trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction. And unlike a political class that tolerated China’s practices, President Trump has taken decisive steps to address them. Let me state firmly and unequivocally tonight that as we work toward a more balanced relationship, our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple. For decades, the American economy has grown too dependent on foreign supply, while China’s has become increasingly reliant on foreign demand. In other words, the United States must produce more of what we consume, while China must consume more of what it produces. Working together, we can strengthen both of our economies without perpetuating the imbalances between them. As Ray Dalio would say, we should have a big, beautiful rebalancing. So, as this President returns the American people to the center of American policy, let me be clear that our renewed emphasis on economic strength does not reflect hostility toward our trading partnerships. On the contrary, we are recovering the purpose that makes each of them worthwhile. After decades of imbalance, we are restoring a spirit of reciprocity for the benefit of both of our peoples. Now, as we work together to address the great questions of the last century, we must also summon the resolve to answer those of the next. In the final months of his life, Henry Kissinger was preoccupied with the challenges of a world he would not live to see. Even at the age of 100, his gaze, characteristically, was fixed on the future. On his last trip, he met with President Xi in Beijing to discuss deeper collaboration. Kissinger had come to believe that the advent of superintelligence could represent a novel class of strategic danger. And he recognized that the obligation of great nations, even—and perhaps especially—those with profound differences, is to find common purpose. So, at President Trump’s direction, we have begun that important work by establishing a new dialogue with China on SI, designed to guard against shared risks and prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems. We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology. Finally, we are establishing a direct channel to ensure that either nation can promptly alert the other to serious incidents involving its SI models. As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management—and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership. As we do so, we should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will not always converge. Those early China watchers of the 1960s understood that the differences between our nations were too profound to ignore. But they also knew that the specter of our estrangement was too great to accept. Generations of leaders have demonstrated their faith in the value of this relationship, dating back to when those enterprising merchants aboard the Empress of China returned to New York Harbor. So I will take as my final words tonight those of Samuel Shaw, who, after a fourteen-month voyage, heralded “that a communication is thus happily opened between us and the Eastern Extreme of the Globe.” The patriots of 1784 opened that passage through commerce. The statesmen of the 1970s widened it through diplomacy. And for six decades, the men and women of this Committee have sustained it through the patient work of bringing our people together. Under President Trump, the United States will carry that work into a new era. We will enlarge the prospects for prosperity on both sides of the Pacific. And, secure in our own strength and unwavering commitment to the American people, we will honor those who first forged this relationship by renewing our resolve to strengthen it. Thank you and congratulations. ###

title: November 9, 2026 - FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk For Immediate Release: November 09, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (a stroke caused by a clot that did not originate in the heart) or a high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), often called a “mini-stroke.” “Stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in the United States, and survivors are at risk of having another stroke,” said Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., MMSc, Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Today’s approval represents a meaningful advance for patients and health care providers seeking a new option for secondary stroke prevention.” The effectiveness of Sunharbo was demonstrated in the OCEANIC-STROKE study , a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study that enrolled 12,327 adults. Participants had a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk TIA and were randomly assigned to Sunharbo or placebo within 72 hours of symptom onset. Both groups also received antiplatelet therapy. Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months. The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment. Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more commonly with Sunharbo compared to placebo. The most frequently reported adverse reaction (occurring in 3% or greater of Sunharbo-treated patients) was diarrhea. Concomitant use with medicines that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (such as carbamazepine) is not recommended because these medicines may decrease Sunharbo’s effectiveness. Sunharbo is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Sunharbo should be withheld at least 24 hours before elective surgery or invasive procedures and for at least 24 hours after thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. The FDA granted Sunharbo Fast Track and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc., Whippany, N.J. November 5, 2026 - FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
body: FDA News Release FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma For Immediate Release: November 05, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies. Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV). Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy. “Today’s approval represents a meaningful step forward for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a disease where treatment options have historically been limited and outcomes remain poor,” said Angelo De Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “This therapy offers patients and their physicians a new option with the potential to make a real difference in people’s lives.” The Accelerated Approval Program allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need based on surrogate or intermediate endpoints. In this case, accelerated approval of Rybrevant Faspro was granted based on overall response rate and duration of response. Since it is not yet confirmed whether this will translate into a clinically meaningful benefit in long-term outcomes, the FDA has required confirmatory studies to verify and describe clinical benefit. In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%, meaning these patients saw their tumor either decrease in size or disappear. Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less and poor outcomes. The prescribing information for use as a single agent includes warnings and precautions for hypersensitivity and administration-related reactions, interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis, dermatologic adverse reactions, ocular toxicity, and harm to an unborn baby. The FDA granted Rybrevant Faspro Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc. title: November 2, 2026 - FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
body: FDA News Release FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality FDA issues final guidance for cell and gene therapy manufacturers, recommends building potency assurance into every stage of a therapy’s lifecycle — from early development through patient delivery For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. "Patients who receive cellular and gene therapies are often battling serious or life-threatening conditions, such as cancers and rare diseases, and they deserve the assurance that the product administered to them will perform as intended," said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research . "This guidance reflects the FDA's commitment to ensuring America remains the best place in the world to innovate — and that innovation is matched by the highest standards of product quality and patient safety." The guidance provides flexible, risk-based recommendations for manufacturers on how to integrate potency considerations at every stage of development and commercialization — from early-phase investigational new drug (IND) submissions through biologics license application (BLA) approval and continued post-market verification. Key topics include controls for variability in raw materials, testing during manufacturing, and lab tests that confirm each batch is biologically active in a way that matches its intended therapeutic effect. The guidance also addresses specialized considerations for products with short shelf lives, viral vector gene therapies, and patient-specific therapies. By giving manufacturers a clear, predictable roadmap, this guidance supports faster access to safe and effective therapies for patients who often have no other treatment options — many of whom receive products made individually for a single person. In doing so, it advances the FDA's public health pillars: protecting patients through rigorous quality standards, promoting innovation by providing regulatory clarity, and reinforcing the integrity of the supply chain for some of the most complex medical products in existence. The FDA will host a webinar on December 10, 2026, to help stakeholders understand and implement the guidance.
